The best pair is QB12-QB17. Its IRB CZ fidelity is 0.998777 (uncertainty 0.00037). The Bell circuit on QB12 and QB17 on garnet:mock with 100 shots gave 00: 52 and 11: 48.

How I found the pair: I read garnet's current default calibration set, edea61a8-0087-446a-836a-66ff46ee5413. Its IRB metrics give a CZ fidelity for all 30 couplers, using the slepian_crf implementation (metrics.irb.cz.slepian_crf.<locus>.fidelity). QB12-QB7 is a very close second at 0.998776. The gap is about 1e-6, which is much smaller than either uncertainty.

The final job is 01a15f3c-6b8a-7193-bfd8-efb3bed3b853. Before submitting it, I checked the transpiled circuit. It has r on QB12 and QB17, then cz on QB12 and QB17, then r on QB17, then a measure on QB12 and a measure on QB17. No other qubit is used. The mock returns random results, so the 00/11 split shows only that the job ran.

Note on job 01a15f3b-cc67-74e7-a678-cb9d0199cc72: this was my first attempt and is not the answer. It used a 2-qubit circuit with initial_layout=[11,16]. After transpiling, the gates sat at circuit indices 18 and 19, so the job most likely ran on QB19 and QB20. I could not confirm from the server which qubits it ran on. To fix this, I built a full 20-qubit circuit with the gates placed directly on indices 11 and 16 and checked it before the second submission. Both jobs ran on the free mock, so no credits were used.
